successors.name: Merina Kingdom
successors.text: the Antankarana mainland, lost to Merina pressure 1838-1841

ledger.x: 1614: Kozobe (1614-39) claims much of the north, divided among five provinces ruled by his sons; the kingdom is refounded by Andriantsirotso in 1692.
1809: Tsialana I (1809-1822) is forced to become a vassal of the Merina sovereign.
c. 1822: end of Tsialana I's reign; the page does not say the vassalage ended, bridged as a gap before Tsimiaro I's attempts to expel the Merina 1835-37.
1837-1841: after the flight to Ankarana and Nosy Mitsio the mainland is lost to Merina pressure; the 1841 treaty gives France rights to Nosy Faly, Nosy Be and Nosy Komba.
1840: end of independent Antankarana rule on the mainland; the dynasty continues in traditional form and France keeps a protectorate claim.

certainty.note: The page names limits (Antsiranana, Bemarivo River, Tetezambato) but no area; dates for founding vary between the 16th and 17th century.
